names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Διονύσιος του Γλουσέτσκ ο Θαυματουργός», with the rank word, the place and the epithet left off.

birth.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε, πιθανόν το 1362 μ.Χ., στα προάστια της πόλεως Βολογκντά της Ρωσίας» — the page's own «πιθανόν», probably, is why the basis is traditional; its heading gives the year without the qualification, «(1362 - 1437)».

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Διονύσιος κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη, το 1437 μ.Χ., σε ηλικία εβδομήντα πέντε ετών.»

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026). saint.gr makes him a Russian abbot of the Vologda country, so the Russian calendar is very likely to keep him; this row says what was read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Διονύσιος του Γλουσέτσκ ο Θαυματουργός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. He is none of the corpus's other Dionysiuses, all of whom are Greek, Egyptian or Romanian; this one is the fifteenth-century founder on the Glushitsa river. `iconographer` is on the page's own word, «Κατείχε, επίσης, το χάρισμα του αγιογράφου», and `abbot` on its account of the two houses he built and governed. No `locations` are entered although the page names several places, because it names them as a route and not as one seat. No hymn is printed for him.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
